title: Ladli Laxmi Yojana MP: Benefits, Eligibility, Apply 2025
meta_description: Ladli Laxmi Yojana MP: Rs 1,43,000 certificate for girl children paid in stages from Class 6 to age 21. Check eligibility and apply at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Madhya Pradesh issues a Rs 1,43,000 certificate for a girl child, released in stages from birth through age 21. Eligibility, payment stages, and how to apply.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Ladli Laxmi Yojana is a Madhya Pradesh government scheme that issues a savings certificate worth Rs 1,43,000 in the name of a girl child at the time of registration. The certificate amount is released progressively in six stages as the girl advances through her education and reaches the age of 21.

The scheme was launched in 2007 by the Women and Child Development Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. It has since been updated under Ladli Laxmi 2.0 to include support for higher education, covering graduation and vocational courses as well.

The scheme's core purpose is to reduce son preference in MP households by giving families a direct financial incentive to educate their daughters. Every stage of the girl's schooling triggers a payment, ensuring that the benefit is connected to her educational progress and not just her birth.

Girls from all communities including General, OBC, SC, and ST categories are eligible for this scheme. There is no income ceiling based on salary or landholding, only the condition that parents must not be income tax payers.

This page covers only Ladli Laxmi Yojana, which is the girl-child education scheme for daughters from birth through higher education. It is a completely different programme from Ladli Behna Yojana, which is the monthly cash transfer scheme for adult women in MP.

The six payment stages add up to Rs 1,43,000 per girl and cover her journey from primary school admission through higher education to adulthood. No single large payment is made at registration; the money is unlocked at each education milestone to ensure continued schooling.

MP parents frequently search for this scheme under several variant spellings including ladli laxmi yojna, ladli lakshmi yojana, lly mp, and lly yojna hindi. All these refer to the same scheme and the same official portal at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in.

The scheme applies to girls born on or after 1 January 2006, which means many girls currently in their teens and early twenties may still have active certificates. Parents who registered daughters years ago should check the current payment status on the official portal.

Since its launch, the scheme has registered millions of girl children across every district of Madhya Pradesh. Its reach across all communities and regions has made Ladli Laxmi Yojana one of the most enrolled government benefit schemes in the Hindi-belt states.

Applications for Ladli Laxmi Yojana can be filed completely free of charge through Anganwadi workers, Lok Seva Kendras, or authorised internet cafes. No agent, intermediary, or application fee is required at any stage of the process.

The dedicated portal at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in allows parents to apply online, download the official certificate, and check the status of each payment stage. The same registration number issued at the time of enrolment is used for all these functions.

The scheme has a well-established certificate system, and the Ladli Laxmi certificate issued at registration is an official government document. This certificate is increasingly accepted as supporting proof of a girl's identity and educational record.

Parents should register their daughter as early as possible after birth to take full advantage of all six payment stages. Delayed registration may still be permitted within a five-year window for certain special categories, but timely registration is strongly recommended.

The scheme does not just cover biological daughters born in conventional family settings. Adopted daughters, orphaned girls, and girls born to women in prison are all covered under special provision clauses of the scheme.

Many families search for information about this scheme using terms like mp ladli laxmi yojna and ladlilaxmi mp gov, reflecting the large number of people across the state actively looking to enrol or track their benefits. The official portal handles all these queries and is kept updated by the department.

The scheme was expanded under Ladli Laxmi 2.0 to add a higher education benefit, recognising that girls who complete Class 12 also need financial support to enter college or a vocational course. This update significantly increased the long-term value of each registered girl's certificate.

Parents who registered a daughter but later misplaced the registration number can retrieve it by searching with the girl's name and date of birth on the official portal. The certificate remains valid and downloadable regardless of how long ago the registration was made.

The scheme has been recognised as a model for girl-child financial support across the Hindi-speaking states. Several other states have since launched their own staged benefit programmes for daughters based on the structure originally developed in MP.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm eligibility before starting
how_to_apply.description: Verify that the girl was born on or after 1 January 2006 and that both parents are original residents (mool niwasi) of Madhya Pradesh. Confirm that the family has two or fewer children and that the parents do not file income tax returns.

how_to_apply.title: Gather the required documents
how_to_apply.description: Collect the girl's birth certificate, a joint photograph showing the girl with both parents, a domicile or residence certificate proving MP residency, and the girl's vaccination card from her Anganwadi or health centre. Having attested copies of all documents is advisable.

how_to_apply.title: Reach your nearest application point
how_to_apply.description: Visit your local Anganwadi worker, the nearest Lok Seva Kendra, or an internet cafe authorised by the MP government to handle this application. The application is submitted entirely free of charge and no payment should be made to anyone at this stage.

how_to_apply.title: Submit the online application
how_to_apply.description: The Anganwadi worker or Lok Seva Kendra operator will enter the application on the official portal at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in on your behalf. After submission, you will receive an application reference number that you should note down carefully for all future follow-up.

how_to_apply.title: Download the Ladli Laxmi certificate
how_to_apply.description: Once the department verifies the application, the official certificate is generated in the girl's name and made available on the portal. Visit ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in/Application/Public/View_Certificatedetails.aspx, enter the registration number, and download the certificate PDF for your records.

how_to_apply.title: Claim each scholarship stage as it falls due
how_to_apply.description: Each time the girl is admitted to Class 6, Class 9, Class 11, or Class 12, log in to the portal or visit the Anganwadi worker to initiate that stage's payment. For the age-21 payout and the higher education instalment, submit the fresh claim with the required proof through the ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in portal.

ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh

extra_sections.title: Ladli Laxmi vs Ladli Behna: Two Completely Different Schemes
extra_sections.content:
Ladli Laxmi Yojana is for girl children from birth, giving staged payments up to Rs 1,43,000 through education. Ladli Behna Yojana is an entirely separate scheme that gives monthly cash transfers to adult women of MP and is already live on this website.

If you are a woman looking for the monthly Rs 1,250 benefit, that is Ladli Behna Yojana, not this page.

extra_sections.heading: Ladli Laxmi Yojana: Payment Stages and Amounts
rows: Rs 6,000 per year for 5 years from registration into the Ladli Laxmi Fund
Graduation or vocational course of 2+ years after Class 12
Appeared in Class 12 board exam; married only after legal age

extra_sections.title: The Final Payout at Age 21
extra_sections.desc:
Released when the girl turns 21, provided she appeared in the Class 12 board exam and married only after the legal age.

This single condition makes Ladli Laxmi one of India's strongest anti-child-marriage incentives, tying the largest payment directly to staying in school and delaying marriage.

extra_sections.heading: Who qualifies
qualify: Girl born on or after 1 January 2006
Both parents are MP mool niwasi (original residents)
Parents are not income tax payers
Family has two or fewer children
First daughter born on/after 1 April 2008 (no family planning condition)
Orphaned, adopted, and triplet girls covered under special provisions
disqualify: Parents not MP residents or without domicile certificate
Either parent is an income tax payer
More than two children without family planning adopted
Girl discontinues studies (future stage payments stop)

steps.title: Register at birth or early
steps.desc: Certificate worth Rs 1,43,000 issued in the girl's name; Rs 30,000 deposited over the first 5 years.

steps.title: Claim at each class
steps.desc: Rs 2,000 at Class 6, Rs 4,000 at Class 9, Rs 6,000 each at Class 11 and 12, actively claimed at each admission.

steps.title: Higher education + age 21
steps.desc: Rs 25,000 for a 2-year-plus course, then Rs 1,00,000 at age 21 after the Class 12 exam.

items.title: Birth cutoff
items.sub: The girl must be born on or after 1 January 2006. Girls born before this date do not qualify under current rules.

items.title: MP residence required
items.sub: Both parents must be mool niwasi of MP. Families without a valid domicile certificate are not eligible.

items.title: First daughter relaxation
items.sub: A first child girl born on/after 1 April 2008 is eligible without any family planning requirement.

items.title: Orphans and adopted girls
items.sub: Orphaned girls are covered through the district WCD officer. Legally adopted daughters are treated the same as biological daughters.

items.title: Single parent and triplets
items.sub: A surviving father can register with a death certificate. Triplet girls at a first delivery are all eligible.

extra_sections.text: A girl registered under Ladli Laxmi Yojana carries a government certificate of Rs 1,43,000 in her name from the day of enrolment. Every class she passes unlocks the next payment, so her academic progress becomes a direct financial event for the family.

items.title: Download the certificate
items.sub: Visit ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in/Application/Public/View_Certificatedetails.aspx and enter the girl's registration number to download the PDF.

items.title: Track status
items.sub: Check application or payment status at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in or shikshaportal.mp.gov.in using the registration number.

items.title: DBT to registered account
items.sub: Each payment is released to the bank account registered at application. Update bank details on the portal before a stage is due if they have changed.

items.title: Claim each stage actively
items.sub: Class 6, 9, 11, and 12 payments must be claimed at the time of each admission. Delaying a claim pushes payment to the next cycle.

extra_sections.heading: Documents Required for Ladli Laxmi Yojana

items.title: Girl's birth certificate
items.sub: The primary proof of the girl's date of birth, which must be on or after 1 January 2006.

items.title: Samagra ID
items.sub: Both the girl's Samagra ID and the family Samagra ID are mandatory for the online application.

items.title: Joint photograph
items.sub: A recent photograph of the girl with a parent is needed at the time of registration.

items.title: Domicile certificate
items.sub: A residence or domicile certificate proving the parents are mool niwasi of Madhya Pradesh.

items.title: Vaccination card
items.sub: The girl's vaccination card from her Anganwadi or health centre.

items.title: Family planning certificate
items.sub: Required for a second girl child, confirming family planning was adopted after her birth.

extra_sections.title: The One-Year Registration Window
extra_sections.content:
The application should be submitted within one year of the girl's birth, and Anganwadi registration is mandatory.

If you miss the one-year window, an appeal can still be made within the next year to the district collector. In special cases, registration is allowed up to the girl's fifth birthday, and a legal guardian can register an orphaned girl within five years.

extra_sections.heading: If a Payment or Application Is Stuck

items.title: Bank details not active
items.sub: Check that the bank account linked to the Samagra ID is correct and active, since DBT payments fail on inactive or wrongly linked accounts.

items.title: Document errors
items.sub: Recheck uploaded documents and correct any errors at the nearest Anganwadi centre or Lok Seva Kendra.

items.title: Samagra mismatch
items.sub: Update Samagra ID information through a Lok Seva Kendra before checking status again, as mismatched family data blocks verification.

items.title: Stage payment delay
items.sub: Each class stage must be claimed at the time of admission. A delayed claim moves the payment to the next processing cycle, so claim promptly.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply: Online and Offline

items.title: Online via portal
items.sub: Visit ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in, select the application type, enter the girl's, parents', and Samagra details, upload documents, and submit. Note the registration number shown.

items.title: Offline via Anganwadi
items.sub: Visit the nearest Anganwadi centre, Lok Seva Kendra, or WCD Project Office, get the form, attach documents, and submit for verification by the Anganwadi worker or project office.

items.title: Verification step
items.sub: The Anganwadi worker, project office, or WCD department verifies the application and documents before registration is approved and the certificate is generated.

items.title: Free of cost
items.sub: The application is free at every stage. No payment should be made to any operator or agent to file it.

extra_sections.title: Why the Scheme Is Structured in Stages
extra_sections.content:
No single large payment is made at registration. The Rs 1,43,000 is unlocked at each education milestone so the benefit stays tied to the girl actually staying in school.

That is also why the final Rs 1,00,000 needs a Class 12 exam appearance and marriage only after legal age. If the girl drops out before Class 6 or marries before 18, the later stage payments stop.

faqs.question: What is Ladli Laxmi Yojana MP?
faqs.answer: Mukhyamantri Ladli Laxmi Yojana is a Madhya Pradesh government scheme that issues a savings certificate of Rs 1,43,000 in the name of a girl child at registration. The amount is released in six stages linked to the girl's education milestones from Class 6 to age 21.

faqs.question: What is the total amount under Ladli Laxmi Yojana and how is it paid?
faqs.answer: The total certificate value is Rs 1,43,000. It is paid as Rs 2,000 at Class 6, Rs 4,000 at Class 9, Rs 6,000 at Class 11, Rs 6,000 at Class 12, Rs 25,000 for higher education in two instalments, and Rs 1,00,000 as a final payout at age 21.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Ladli Laxmi Yojana in Madhya Pradesh?
faqs.answer:
Apply free of charge through your local Anganwadi worker, at a Lok Seva Kendra, or at an authorised internet cafe. You need the girl's birth certificate, a family photograph, a domicile certificate, and her vaccination card.

No fee should be paid to anyone.

faqs.question: What is the official portal for Ladli Laxmi Yojana registration?
faqs.answer: The official portal is ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in. You can apply, download the Ladli Laxmi certificate, and check payment status on this portal using the registration number issued at the time of enrolment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Ladli Laxmi and Ladli Behna Yojana MP?
faqs.answer:
Ladli Laxmi Yojana is for girl children from birth, providing staged payments up to Rs 1,43,000 through education. Ladli Behna Yojana is a completely different scheme that gives monthly cash payments to adult women of MP.

The two have no overlap in eligibility or purpose.

faqs.question: How do I download the Ladli Laxmi Yojana certificate?
faqs.answer: Visit ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in/Application/Public/View_Certificatedetails.aspx and enter the girl's registration number. The certificate PDF will be available for download once the department has approved the application.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for Ladli Laxmi Yojana?
faqs.answer:
The girl must be born on or after 1 January 2006. Her parents must be original residents (mool niwasi) of MP, must not be income tax payers, and must have two or fewer children.

If she is the second child, parents must have adopted family planning after her birth.

faqs.question: How do I check my Ladli Laxmi Yojana status online?
faqs.answer: Visit ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in or shikshaportal.mp.gov.in and enter the registration number in the status check section. The portal shows the current application status and whether each stage payment has been released or is pending.

faqs.question: When does Ladli Laxmi Yojana give Rs 1 lakh?
faqs.answer: The Rs 1,00,000 final payout is released when the girl turns 21, provided she has appeared in the Class 12 board examination. If the girl married before age 21, the marriage must have taken place after the minimum legal age under the Child Marriage Prohibition Act 2006.

faqs.question: Is Ladli Laxmi Yojana available for a second daughter?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The scheme covers the first and second daughters in a family.

For the second daughter, the parents must have adopted family planning measures after her birth for the family to remain eligible.

faqs.question: What is lly yojna hindi and lly mp?
faqs.answer:
Lly yojna hindi and lly mp are short-form search terms used in Madhya Pradesh to refer to Ladli Laxmi Yojana. LLY stands for Ladli Laxmi Yojana.

All information about this scheme, in Hindi and English, is available at ladlilaxmi.mp.gov.in.

faqs.question: Can an orphaned girl apply for Ladli Laxmi Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Orphaned girls are eligible under special provisions of the scheme.

The district Women and Child Development officer or Anganwadi supervisor handles the registration process on behalf of the orphaned child.
